newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SRINATH BOWLS INDIA TO VICTORY AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRINATH BOWLS INDIA TO VICTORY AGAINST SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Indian pace bowler Javagal Srinath turned in a career-best bowling performance on Saturday to spur India to a 64-run victory over South Africa in the first cricket test.
The Indian pacer, named man of the match, took six wickets for 21 runs in 11.5 overs as the visitors collapsed for 105, chasing a victory target of 170.
Leg-spinner Anil Kumble played a fine supporting role, taking three wic 34 runs in 12 overs.
Srinath struck in his very first over, taking wickets off successive deliveries to have South Africa reeling at nought for two.
The lanky Srinath took two wickets off successive deliveries three times in thengs.

On a wearing wicket extending considerable help to spin bowlers, the visitors were expected to struggle against the Indian spinners but no-one could have predicted their sensational collapse against a pace bowler.
Six South Africans failed to open their accounts.
At lunch, the visitors seemed to be fairly safe at 48 for three. But in a dramatic post-lunch session, they lost their last six wickets for only nine runs in 25 balls.
Only South African skipper Hansie Cronje showed the willingness to stay at the wicket and fight the odds, compiling an unbeaten 48.
The next highest scores were Gary Kirsten's 20 and extras with nine.
The South African second innings failed to last even two full sessions of play.
For the Indians, this was the second consecutive victory in tests, after they beat Australia recently in a one-off test in New Delhi.
Earlier, the Indian second innings, resuming at the overnight score of 172 for seven, folded up for 190 within half an hour of the start of play.
Left arm spinner Paul Adams took all the three Indian wickets to fall on Saturday to finish with figures of three for 30. Allan Donald took three for 32.
The second test match starts in Calcutta on November 27.
